title: Simultaneous Bands for Sorted Treatment Effects near a Quartically Flat Maximum
banked_reason: Completed D0.5 math PASS and eleven cited sources verified-attested; authoritative novelty tier incremental below field, paper_score_ceiling 6 < 7.4, not salvageable within scope.
gap_reasons: The delivered result is an estimator-specific critical-bandwidth process law under known scalar design, exact quartic flatness, and global peak separation; it establishes neither optimal precision nor adaptation beyond that geometry.

Asymptotic computability does not establish operational usefulness: the prescribed simulation budgets force the full-range fallback bands for every n up to 10^28, and no delivered experiment demonstrates useful finite-sample calibration.
tldr: The full known-uniform binary observational benchmark admits a finite original-record estimator whose shrinking upper-tail error curve converges uniformly to a quartic-drift Gaussian excursion inverse, including a non-Gaussian maximum. Consistent observable curvature and residual scale, an exact quartic simulated drift, and certified finite numerical and Monte Carlo budgets yield connected simultaneous \(90\%\) bands. The critical values are bounded by the public constant \(402\) with class-uniform probability tending to one.
gap: Regular sorted-effect limit theory excludes critical values. Pointwise rough-nuisance CATE rates leave the joint endpoint covariance undetermined. Broad CATE-distribution inference already exists.
